summary: The contract fixes every date to five characters in one 365-day non-leap year, so converting four dates and intersecting two intervals has no scalable input dimension and matches the constant output cost.

optimality.argument: A correct call must inspect enough fixed-format date fields to distinguish overlapping from disjoint stays and emit one integer, requiring Omega(1) work. Four fixed-length ordinal conversions and constant-many comparisons achieve O(1).

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required integer decision and distinguishing at least one overlapping contract from one disjoint contract requires Omega(1) work.
The accepted source converts four five-character dates with one fixed 12-entry prefix table and intersects their ordinal intervals using a constant number of operations.
Regression checks all 133225 pairs of single-day stays, every legal interval against full-year and endpoint-day stays, and deterministic interval pairs against an independent set-intersection oracle.
